item.title: Qt, Linux and everything: Debugging Qt WebAssembly
item.description:
Emscripten embeds DWARF symbols in the wasm binaries. NOTE: Debugging wasm files with DWARF works only in the Chrome browser with the help of a browser extension. The javascript console will soon contain file source file paths and sources.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 4 Comments:

N_Lens:

What's interesting here is that you can now debug WebAssembly applications with full C++ source-level debugging directly in Chrome, complete with breakpoints, variable inspection, and step-through debugging, just like a native desktop app.

What makes this particularly interesting is the technology stack: Emscripten embeds DWARF debugging symbols (the same format used for native Linux binaries) directly into WebAssembly binaries. A Chrome browser extension then reads these embedded symbols and reconstructs the original C++ source code view in the DevTools, mapping the compiled WebAssembly back to your Qt C++ source with full directory paths intact.

All of this would have seemed impossible not long ago.

irishcoffee:

I feel like this article is severely flawed.

Debugging wasm qt apps is not hard at all. Yes, as the article says, you need to build the code in debug mode, this isn’t unusual.

If you use qtcreator, it’s, and I hate this word, trivial. Most of the work comes from setting up the qt kit in qtcreator… which takes about 5 minutes.

Breakpoints just work. Debugging just works. Everything… works.

oblio:

Is anyone using Qt for developing Mac apps these days? How is the integration after the recent Mac UI refresh?

em3rgent0rdr:

Very useful. It would be great for the browser become the cross-platform application target. I've been eagerly waiting for Qt WebAssembly to mature.

item.title: OpenEvolve: Teaching LLMs to Discover Algorithms Through Evolution
item.description:
Candidate programs are produced via LLM-guided edits (diff-based by default), evaluated with user-defined metrics, and organized using MAP-Elites while an island model with migration supports parallel, diversified exploration. Program Database: Implements MAP-Elites per island, binning programs along configurable feature dimensions (defaults include complexity and diversity; custom dimensions are taken from evaluator metrics). Cascade Evaluation Evaluation proceeds in stages with configurable thresholds.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 4 Comments:

quantbagel:

Sakana.ai improved on this by honing in on sample efficiency iirc with shinkaevolve (which is open source and not an ai slop project)

N_Lens:

Some cool optimisations here: MAP elites, island models to prevent premature convergence & fast rejection of bad candidates.

What's particularly interesting is the meta level insight: The system discovered scipy.optimize.SLSQP for circle packing - a completely different algorithmic paradigm than it started with. It's genuinely discovering new approaches, not just parameter-tuning.

DoctorOetker:

Very interesting that the LLM weights are co-evolved and reasoning skills improve!

jasonjmcghee:

It doesn't mention it in the article, but guessing this is based on / inspired by AlphaEvolve?

Though I'm not sure the public can access AlphaEvolve yet.

(https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131)
